# frontend

```go
import "github.com/lucasavila00/tgo/internal/frontend"
```

Package frontend reads TGo source into native syntax nodes.

The parser reads the complete source once. A postfix operator belongs to its actual operand. An if expression owns its branches. A comprehension owns its written outputs and clauses. The checker and lowerer use these same nodes, so types, bindings, and error positions refer to the source that the user wrote.

Value branches and collection clauses belong to the enclosing source function. Returns, defers, and jumps keep that function's meaning. A function literal appears in the tree only when the source contains a function literal.

Physical file names select Go build inputs. Logical source names and line directives identify diagnostics. Both use the original input positions. The frontend also saves source call text for the context added by \!\!.

## type Parsed

Parsed holds source syntax and the call names used in propagated error context.

```go
type Parsed struct {
    File      *ast.File
    CallNames map[*ast.PropagateExpr]string
}
```

### func ParseFile

```go
func ParseFile(fset *token.FileSet, filename, sourceName string, input []byte) (*Parsed, error)
```

ParseFile reads native TGo syntax using the physical file and logical source name.
